relevance_note: Case report of one girl with a TNFAIP3 deletion and HA20: "a novel de novo 119 kb microdeletion containing only TNFAIP3"; Table 1 also summarizes four previously published HA20 patients with TNFAIP3 deletions.
method_note: Read the whole paper including the converted Supplementary Table S1 (labs of the patient at 8 months). Table 1 has patients as columns (header row label 'Location'); column 1 is 'This report' (the index patient, labelled 'patient' and given the Table 1 column 1 data), columns 2-5 are previously published patients labelled 'Table 1 column 2'..'Table 1 column 5' (refs Shimizu et al.^10, Tsuchida et al.^8 x2, Franco-Jarava et al.^9). A short Python script built the JSON and cut Table 1 row segments (row label through the patient's cell) and supplement-table spans from the paper text; I checked its output against the tables. Parents are in scope as tested relatives: mother II-2 and father II-1 (no TNFAIP3 variant rows for them). Grandparents were tested (DNA extracted, pedigree in Fig. 1D) but no individual-level result is printed in the text, and their number is not stated, so they got no rows. The TNFAIP3 c.305A>G (NM_001270507.2) variant (apparently homozygous in the patient, heterozygous in the mother, absent in the father) is described by the authors as relatively common (MAF = 0.0117) and used only as a marker revealing the deletion; it was left out as a common non-causal variant. Deletion size differs by method: EXCAVATOR2 on WES data reported a 187 kb microdeletion 'within the TNFAIP3 gene', the SNP array a 119 kb microdeletion 'involving only TNFAIP3'; the 119 kb SNP-array result (also in Table 1) was recorded. De novo is taken from the stated CNV analysis of the patient and both parents (Supplementary Fig. S1 legend) plus the SNP array of patient and father; the mother's deletion-negative result is implied by 'de novo' rather than printed separately. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27): rheumatoid factor, T-SPOT, EBV-IgM/IgG, C7-HRP, stool culture; esophagogastroduodenoscopy 'unremarkable', terminal ileum 'normal' and the immunological workup 'no apparent abnormalities' are whole examinations and are written as the paper names them, excluding nothing more specific. Lab values above the printed normal range (IL-6, sTNFR-1, sTNFR-2, IL-18, ESR, speckled ANA 80x) were recorded as observed elevations; HLA-B51/A26 negative typing, the WBC count (no normal range printed) and the 1-month screening 'not consistent with primary immunodeficiency, autoinflammatory disease, or hemophagocytic syndrome' were not recorded as features. Age 8 months is recorded as age at diagnosis (Table 1); age at last evaluation is not stated (seton drainage continued for 1 year), so it is not reported. Hepatosplenomegaly was not mapped to the lymphoproliferation checklist item. Perianal ulcers (Table 1 columns 2 and 5) were counted under gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation; 'thyroiditis' (column 4) was not counted as autoimmune thyroiditis because the paper does not call it autoimmune. n_patients_reported = 5 from 'five of 69 ... carried a deletion', matching the five Table 1 patients. No contradictions found.
